questions.question: A circle inscribed in a triangle ABC touches its sides AB, BC and AC at the points D, E and F, respectively. If AB = 18 cm, BC = 15 cm and AC = 13 cm, then the value of AD + BE + CF is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AB = 18 cm, BC = 15 cm and AC = 13 cm,

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/84855d223b5536c89f09a37450f6e94117a76a7b21031b8f21f0da4bcc8b465f.png] 

We know, AD = AF, DB = BE, CE = FC

The perimeter of the triangle = AB + BC + AC = 18 + 15 + 13 = 46

That is, AD + AF + BD + BE + CE + CF = 46

Or, 2 × (AD + BE + CF) = 46

**∴ AD + BE + CF = 23**

questions.question:
In the figure, L is the centre of the circle, and ML is the perpendicular to LN. If the area of the triangle MLN is 36, then the area of the circle is:

questions.solution:
**Given:**

L is the center of the circle and ML is perpendicular to LN

Area of the triangle MLN = 36

**Formula:**

Area of the circle = πr²

Area of the right-angled triangle = (1/2) × Base × Height

**Calculation:**

In ΔLMN

LM = LN = r (Radius of the circle)

Area of right-angled ΔLMN = (1/2) × r × r

⇒ 36 = r²/2

⇒ r² = 72

∴ Area of the circle = πr² = 72π

questions.question: If angle subtended by a chord on the major arc of a circle is 55 degree, then what will be the angle subtended by the same chord on the centre of the circle?
questions.solution:
Given:

The angle subtended by a chord on the major arc of a circle is 55 degrees.

Concept used:

The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d1c05989f2a0fa189db04629cea60370d1cee997bed9ae58452c4c12110f967d.png] 

Let O, R, and PQ be the centre, a point on the major arc, and the aforementioned chord respectively.

So, the major arc for the PQ chord is PRQ.

Hence, ∠PRQ = 55°

Here, ∠POQ is the angle subtended by the same chord, PQ on the centre of the circle.

According to the concept,

∠POQ = 2 × ∠PRQ

⇒ ∠POQ = 2 × 55°

⇒ ∠POQ = 110°

**∴ The angle subtended by the same chord on the centre of the circle is 110°.**

questions.question: The ratio in which a transverse common tangent drawn to two circles with radii 4 cm and 6 cm, respectively, divides the line joining their centres is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the circles are 4 cm and 6 cm.

**Concept used:**

If two triangles are similar then the ratio of the corresponding sides of the triangles are equal.

**Calculations:**

Let us draw two circles with centre O and centre M and radius 4 cm and 6 cm respectively.

And the transverse common tangent touches the circle with centre O at A and touches circle having centre M at B and the transverse tangent and line joining A and B meets at C.

So, AO = 4 cm and BM = 6 cm

Now, In ∆AOC and ∆BMC, We have:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1a428c2467d5abae0238fecc236dd4fbff95cb34b795c2543e7f5dfaa3d6c43d.png] 

Rightarrow Angle A = Angle B = 90°( tangent and radius at same point are perpendicular to each other)

Rightarrow Angle AOC = Angle BMC ( OA and MB are perpendicular to the same line AB. So, OA || MB, Thus, by alternate angle theorem Angle AOC = Angle BMC)

Hence, ∆AOC ≈ ∆BMC

therefore, (AO)/(BM)=(OC)/(MC)= (4)/(6) =(2)/(3)

**Hence, The Required ratio is 2 : 3.**

questions.question: Two circles touch each other externally at any point C. PQ is the direct common tangent to both the circles touching the circles at point P and point Q. If the radii of the circles are 36 cm and 16 cm, respectively, then the length of PQ is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of 1st circle = 36 cm

Radius of 2nd circle = 16 cm

**Formula used:**

If two circle touches each other externally and a common tangent is passing then,

Length of common tangent = √(4 × r₁ × r₂)

**Calculation:**

Length of common tangent (PQ) = √(4 × 36 × 16)

⇒ 2 × 6 × 4 = 48 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.**

questions.question: Distance of a chord JK from the centre is 7 cm. If diameter of this circle is 50 cm, then what will be length of this chord?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a circle, the **radius**, **distance from center**, and **half-chord length** form a **right-angled triangle**.

Radius (r) = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 cm. Distance (d) = 7 cm.

Using the **Pythagorean triplet** (7, 24, 25):

Half-chord length = 24 cm.

Length of chord **JK** = 2 × 24 = 48 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Diameter of the circle = 50 cm

Distance of chord **JK** from centre (**O**) = 7 cm

**Formula Used:**

Radius (r) = Diameter ÷ 2

In ▵**OMJ** (Right-angled), **OJ² = OM² + MJ²** (Pythagoras Theorem)

Chord length **JK** = 2 × **MJ** (Perpendicular from center bisects the chord)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/86d7329b3da31f25dc3ac04003c489f57acd3c903ee6907c5ae688bbee67bd56.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Radius (r) = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 cm

⇒ In right ▵**OMJ**, **OJ** = 25 cm and **OM** = 7 cm

⇒ **MJ²** = **OJ²** − **OM²**

⇒ **MJ²** = 25² − 7²

⇒ **MJ²** = 625 − 49 = 576

⇒ **MJ** = √576 = 24 cm

⇒ Total length of chord **JK** = 2 × **MJ**

⇒ **JK** = 2 × 24 = 48 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perpendicular Bisector Property

A perpendicular drawn from the center of a circle to a chord always bisects the chord into two equal segments.

Pythagorean Triplets

Sets of three integers that satisfy a² + b² = c², such as (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (7, 24, 25), and (8, 15, 17), are extremely useful for quick circle calculations.

Chord Distance Relation

Chords that are equidistant from the center of a circle are equal in length, and longer chords are closer to the center.</p

questions.question: PX is a tangent drawn from point X, touches the circle at P, O is the centre of the circle. Radius of this circle is 10 cm and OX = 26 cm. What is the length of PX ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

PX is a tangent drawn from point X.

O is the centre of the circle.

Radius of this circle is 10 cm and OX = 26 cm.

**Concept Used:**

When a tangent is drawn from an external point to a circle, it forms a right angle with the radius drawn to the point of tangency.

Pythagoras theorem

Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6ee89817c09fc0578f923eafdd8cdd8eef34a8343800d5abe4a7c72a518ea676.png] 

Here PX is the tangent makes 90° angle with the radius.

In triangle OPX,

OP = 10 cm

OX = 26 cm

Apply Pythagoras theorem

Hypotenuse2 = Base2 + Perpendicular2

262 = 102 + Perpendicular2

Perpendicular² = 262 - 102 

Perpendicular2 = 676 - 100

Perpendicular2 = 576

Perpendicular = 24 cm

PX = 24 cm

**∴ Option 2 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: Sum of the angles made by a chord at the centre and on the major arc of a circle is 225 degree. What will be the angle made at the major arc of this circle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **angle subtended by a chord at the centre** is always **twice** the angle subtended by it on the **major arc**.

Ratio of **Angle at Centre** : **Angle on Major Arc** = 2 : 1

Total Ratio Units = 2 + 1 = 3 units

Given: 3 units = 225°

1 unit = 225° ÷ 3 = 75°

**∴ The correct answer is 75 degree.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of **angle at the centre** and **angle on the major arc** = 225°.

**Formula Used:**

Angle subtended by an **arc** at the **centre** is **double** the angle subtended by it at any point on the **remaining part** of the circle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca177ea910ffc214ff95531146fdf7b9fb312e07664414406ce7b254e4277138.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the angle subtended by the chord at the **major arc** be x.

⇒ Angle subtended at the **centre** = 2x

⇒ x + 2x = 225°

⇒ 3x = 225°

⇒ x = 225° ÷ 3

⇒ x = 75°

**∴ The correct answer is 75 degree.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inscribed Angle Theorem

The angle subtended by an arc at the center is exactly twice the angle subtended by the same arc at any point on the circle's circumference (major arc).

Angles in the Same Segment

Angles subtended by the same chord or arc at different points on the same segment (major or minor) of the circle are always equal.

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

The sum of the angle at the major arc and the angle at the minor arc subtended by the same chord is 180°, as they form opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral.</p

questions.question: Two parallel chords are drawn in a circle of radius 25 cm. The distance between the two chords is 27 cm. If the length of one chord is 48 cm, then length of the other chord is equal to:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the circle = 25 cm.

Distance between the two chords = 27 cm.

Length of one chord = 48 cm.

**Formula Used:**

For a chord of length 2l at a distance d from the center in a circle of radius R :

l = sqrt{R² - d²}

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/42095499b7447de3a7f32db41dc2b9698a7cc69649845780bd0a1862a7f21fb8.png] 

Let the two chords be AB and CD with AB = 48 cm and CD = x cm.

Distance of AB from the center OM = d₁

Distance of CD from the center ON = d₂

Given, d₁ + d₂ = 27 cm

Half of AB = 24 cm

Half of CD = x/2 cm

Using the formula for chord length:

24 = sqrt{25² - d₁²}

x/2 = sqrt{25² - d₂²}

Solving for d₁ :

24 = sqrt{625 - d₁²}

Squaring both sides:

⇒ 24² = 625 - d₁²

⇒ 576 = 625 - d₁²

⇒ d₁² = 625 - 576

⇒ d₁² = 49

⇒ d₁ = 7 cm

Since d₁ + d₂ = 27 :

⇒ d₂ = 27 - 7

⇒ d₂ = 20 cm

Using d₂ to find x:

x/2 = sqrt{625 - 20²}

⇒ x/2 = sqrt{625 - 400}

⇒ x/2 = √225

⇒ x/2 = 15

⇒ x = 30 cm

**The length of the other chord is 30 cm.**

questions.question: AB is a chord of a circle in minor segment with center O. C is a point on the minor arc of the circle between the points A and B. The tangents to the circle at A and B meet at the point P. If ∠ACB = 102°, then what is the measure of ∠APB?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∠ACB = 102°

**Concept Used:**

When a quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle, the opposite angles of it are supplementary angles.

The angle subtended at the center is always double the angle subtended at the remaining arc.

The radius from the center of the circle to the point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent line.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/de65049b8c3dd4028c6097d211f1fd07850639d986ab92b325f48aa2bd17d051.png] 

Point D is taken on the major arc of the circle. Then, A & D, B & D, C & B, and A & C are joined.

∠ACB = 102°

Now,

∠ADB = (180 – 102)° = 78°

Now,

∠AOB = (78 × 2)° = 156°

Since OA = OB, ΔAOB is an isosceles triangle and ∠OBA = ∠OAB.

Now,

∠AOB + ∠OBA + ∠OAB = 180°

⇒ 2 × ∠OBA = (180 – 156)°

⇒ ∠OBA = 12°

Now,

∠OBA = 12°

∠OAB = 12°

Now,

∠OAP = ∠OAB + ∠BAP

⇒ 90° = 12° + ∠BAP

⇒ ∠BAP = 78°

Now,

∠OBP = ∠OBA + ∠ABP

⇒ 90° = 12° + ∠ABP

⇒ ∠ABP = 78°

Now,

∠APB + ∠ABP + ∠BAP = 180°

⇒ ∠APB + 78° + 78° = 180°

⇒ ∠APB = 180° - (2 × 78)°

⇒ ∠APB = 24°

**∴ The required measure of ∠APB is 24°.**

 24 = sqrt{d²-(16-6)²}

questions.question: Two circles of radii 8 cm and 3 cm, respectively, are 13 cm apart. AB is a direct common tangent touch to both the circles at A and B respectively then the length of AB is

**GIVEN:**

Distance between them is 13 cm 

AB is a direct common tangent

**FORMULA USED:**

Length of the direct common tangent = sqrt {d² - ( r1 - r2)²}

Where, d= distance between the circles 

r₁ and r₂ are the radii of the two circles respectively

**CALCULATION:**

⇒ sqrt {13² - ( 8 -3)²} = sqrt {144} = 12 cm

questions.question: In a circle with centre O, PA and PB are tangents to the circle at point A and point B, respectively. C is a point on the major arc AB. If ∠ACB = 50°, then find the measure of ∠APB.
questions.solution:
Given:

In a circle with centre O, PA and PB are tangents to the circle at point A and point B, respectively. C is a point on the major arc AB.

∠ACB = 50°

Concept used:

The angle subtended by an arc of a circle at its centre is twice the angle subtended by it at any point of the alternate segment of the circle.

The Sum of all internal angles of a quadrilateral is 360°.

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f60bab58ee0578b7110c56597fe0f49ef282e462f61bb160c6ff2402caa1a444.png] 

According to the concept,

∠AOB = 2 × ∠ACB

⇒ ∠AOB = 2 × 50°

⇒ ∠AOB = 100°

Consider the quadrilateral AOBP, 

∠A + ∠O + ∠B + ∠P = 360°

⇒ 90° + 100° + 90° + ∠P = 360°

⇒ ∠P = 360° - 90° - 90° - 100°

⇒ ∠P = 80°

⇒ ∠APB = 80°

**∴ The measure of ∠APB is 80°.**

questions.question: Chords AB and CD of a circle, when produced, meet at a point P outside the circle. If AB = 6 cm, CD = 3 cm and PD = 5 cm, then PB is equal to:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Chords AB and CD of a circle, when produced, meet at a point P outside the circle. If AB = 6 cm, CD = 3 cm and PD = 5 cm

**Calculation:**

PA × PB = PC × PD

(6 + x) x = 8 × 5

⇒ x² + 6x - 40 = 0

⇒ x² + 10x - 4x - 40

⇒ (x + 10) (x - 4) = 0

⇒ x = 4

**∴ PB is equal to 4 cm.**

questions.question: The angle subtended by a chord AB on the circumference of a circle is 90 degrees. If the length of chord AB is 16 cm, what will be this circle's radius be?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The length of chord AB is 16 cm.

**Concept used:**

If an angle subtended by a chord on the circumference of a circle is 90 degrees, then the chord is the circle's diameter. 

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/be783add49e86069063967881cb0c3e48329445c37301c9db14e1ecdaacfe2fd.png] 

Let O be the circle's center, and let C is the point on the circumference.

Using, If an angle subtended by a chord on the circumference of a circle is 90 degrees, then the chord is the circle's diameter. 

So, AB is the diameter.

The radius is half of the diameter.

AB = 2(OA) = 2(OB) 

⇒ (OA) = (OB) = AB/2 = 16/2

⇒ 8 cm

**∴ Option 1 is the correct answer.**

questions.question:
In the given figure O is the centre of the circle. If angle PRQ = 64°, then what is the measure of angle OPQ?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/37f9abafbb7925b35b247ce1bda8d5a71ce32b5432bdaa75b9ec9fe6e495d309.png]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∠PRQ=64°

**Concept Used:**

Angles opposite to equal sides are equal.

The sum of the angles of a triangle is 180°.

**Formula Used:**

θ = α/2

where θ → Angle made by a chord at circumference of a circle,

α → Angle made by the same chord at the center of the circle

**Calculations:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/37f9abafbb7925b35b247ce1bda8d5a71ce32b5432bdaa75b9ec9fe6e495d309.png] 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

Let ∠POQ = x, ∠OPQ = y

Chord PQ makes ∠PRQ at the circumference and ∠POQ at center of circle.

⇒ ∠POQ = 2 × 64° 

⇒ x = 128° 

In ΔPOQ,

OP = OQ

⇒ ∠OPQ = ∠OQP = y

Now, In ΔPOQ, 

∠ POQ + ∠OPQ + ∠OQP = 180° 

⇒ 128° + y + y = 180° 

⇒ 2y = 180° – 128° 

⇒ y = 52°/2

⇒ y = 26° 

**∴ The value of ∠OPQ is 26°.**

questions.question: In a circle, chords PQ and TS are produced to meet at R. if RQ = 14.4 cm, PQ = 11.2 cm, and SR = 12.8 cm, then the length of chord TS is:

Now, TS = RT – RS = 28.8 – 12.8 = **16 cm.**

questions.question: The length of a chord is 40 cm. If the angle subtended by this chord at the circumference of the circle is 90 degrees. then what will be the radius of this circle?
questions.solution:
Given:

The length of the chord is 40 cm.

Concept used:

If an angle subtended by a chord on the circumference of a circle is 90 degrees, then the chord is the circle's diameter. 

The diameter is the double radius.

Calculation:

questions.question: The length of a common external tangent to two circles of an equal radius of 5 units is equal to the diameter of the circle. Which of the following can be the distance between the centres of the circles in units?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The radii of both circles are equal to 5 units, and the length of the common external tangent is equal to the diameter of the circle, which is 10 units.

**Formula Used:**

The formula for the length of the direct common tangent between two circles of radii r₁ and r₂, and the distance between their centers, d, is:

l = √(d² - (r₁ - r₂)²)

Where:

l = length of the common external tangent

d = distance between the centers of the two circles

r₁ and r₂ = radii of the two circles

**Calculation:**

In this case, both radii are equal, so r₁ = r₂ = 5 units. The length of the common external tangent, l, is equal to the diameter of the circle, i.e., l = 10 units.

Now, substitute the values into the formula:

10 = √(d² - (5 - 5)²)

10 = √(d²)

10² = d²

100 = d²

d = √100 = 10 units

**The distance between the centers of the circles is 10 units.**

questions.question: Two circles of radius of 6 cm each. They intersect each other such that each passes through the centre of the other. What is the length of the common chord?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When two circles of equal radius (r) pass through each other's centre, the length of their common chord is given directly by the formula √3r.

Given, radius (r) = 6 cm.

Length of common chord = 6√3 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 6√3 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 Length of Common Chord PQ

**Given:**

Radius of both circles = r = 6 cm

The circles pass through each other's centre, implying the distance between their centres is exactly equal to their radius.

Distance between centres (AB) = 6 cm

**Concept Used:**

The line joining the centres of two intersecting circles acts as a perpendicular bisector to their common chord.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the centres of the two circles be A and B, and their intersection points be P and Q.

⇒ The distance AP = BP = r = 6 cm.

⇒ The distance AB = r = 6 cm.

⇒ Thus, ΔAPB is an equilateral triangle with a side length of 6 cm.

⇒ Let M be the point of intersection of the common chord PQ and the line AB.

⇒ Since PQ is perpendicularly bisected by AB, AM = AB ÷ 2 = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm.

⇒ In right-angled triangle ΔAMP, using the Pythagoras theorem:

⇒ AP² = AM² + PM²

⇒ 6² = 3² + PM²

⇒ 36 = 9 + PM²

⇒ PM² = 36 − 9 = 27

⇒ PM = √27 = 3√3 cm

⇒ The common chord PQ is exactly twice the length of PM.

⇒ PQ = 2 × PM = 2 × 3√3 = 6√3 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 6√3 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Properties of Common Chord

The common chord of two intersecting circles is perpendicularly bisected by the straight line joining their centres. The maximum length of a common chord equals the diameter of the smaller circle.

Distance Between Centres of Intersecting Circles

If two circles with radii r₁ and r₂ intersect at two distinct points, the distance 'd' between their centres will always satisfy the strict inequality: |r₁ − r₂| < d < r₁ + r₂.

Number of Common Tangents

When two circles intersect each other at exactly two distinct points, exactly 2 direct common tangents can be drawn touching both circles, and no transverse common tangents exist.
